purpose: Scores whether the reviewer's OUTPUT follows the Output Contract in reference/code-review-checklist.md — not whether the right findings fired. Reuses bespoke/ fixtures rather than carrying its own, since format only needs one case with findings and one without, and bespoke already has both — no need for a third copy of similar code.
grading_note: Graded programmatically against the checks below. Each check is pass/fail; a case passes only if all checks pass.

checks.rule: Lines matching ^Scope:, ^Date:, ^Branch:, ^Ticket:, ^Verdict: all present, in that relative order, before the Summary line.
Verdict is consistent with Summary counts per the Verdict Criteria table: any 🔴 → FAIL; no 🔴 but ≥1 🟡 → PASS WITH WARNINGS; otherwise → PASS.
Every finding block starts with 🔴/🟡/🔵 then 'Rule: <section>/<slug>', followed by 'File: <path>:<line>', 'Issue:' and 'Fix:' lines.

Every 'Rule:' value matches a bolded slug under the correspondingly-named section in reference/code-review-checklist.md — no invented rule names — and its severity emoji matches the one tagged on that checklist line.
A 'Recommendations' section, if present, contains independent next steps — not padded boilerplate restating the findings, and not present at all when there's nothing beyond the findings.

cases.note: Reuses bespoke's silent-failure violation — a clear single 🔴 → Verdict FAIL. Tests the full contract under a non-trivial finding set.

Reuses bespoke's resource-lifecycle clean control — expect Summary: 🔴 0 🟡 0 🔵 0 → Verdict PASS. Tests whether the model still emits a well-formed Header/Summary on a zero-finding review, and correctly omits a padded Recommendations section.
